_comment: Config keys only the HOST process may write, and what dropping them does.
Every config.save that arrives over the hub bus — a remote/web client, a plugin,
or an agent through the MCP facade — is by definition not from the host, so these
are stripped before the merge. `updates` earns its place: updates.channel is
concatenated into the electron-updater feed URL the desktop then downloads and
installs from, so one '../' in a channel relocates the updater to somebody else's
repo — persistent code execution laundered through the app's own update dialog.
TWO shapes, because two different things need protecting:
`sections` — a whole top-level key goes or stays (updates).
`paths`    — a dotted SUB-key goes, and its siblings stay. agents.binaries is
the launcher path handed to claudemon's Command::new for every
spawned agent, i.e. argv[0]. It sits inside `agents`, which also
carries ordinary user settings a bus client legitimately edits, so
a section-level drop is the wrong granularity: it would either
leave argv[0] writable (the shipped state) or break every other
agents.* setting over the bus. Pair it with an fs.write over an
existing executable in the caller's own agent cwd — os.WriteFile
and writeFileSync both preserve the 0755 mode — and config.save
alone was arbitrary host code execution on the next spawn.
Both bus entry points must agree: the Go brain (dropHostTrusted, the default under
DELEGATE_CATALOG_TO_BRAIN) and the desktop's own bus handler (hubCapabilities.ts).
The desktop's in-process Settings write does NOT go through either and is unaffected.
THE BLOCK REGISTRY. Every array-of-objects block in this file must be declared
here and everything here must be a block — closure in both directions, so a new
block is a failure until someone says what its cases must carry, and a renamed
one cannot quietly stop being validated.
Held by cmd/brain/corpusvocab_test.go and
apps/desktop/src/main/services/contractsVocabulary.test.ts. Before those, this
kind of validation existed for exactly ONE block of ONE fixture.
